implementation.argument_surface: one 4-byte ordinary stack argument, the receiver, at entry-ESP + 0x4. The incoming ECX is dead: the record's own observation list shows ECX first as REG_READ at index 10, after a definite REG_WRITE at index 2, so nothing between entry and 01053db5 reads it. No other stack slot is read anywhere in the body.
implementation.receiver_model: opaque byte-addressed block. No member of OpaqueBeamToolState, OpaqueBeamTarget or OpaqueBeamTargetVTable is named anywhere in this package, and no size is asserted for any of them: no record for this target says which member any displacement is, and the machine-derived receiver record abstains (offsets == [], register == null, present == null). Every access is spelled as an opaque 4-byte word at a stated machine displacement.
implementation.dispatch_model: one indirect transfer at 0x01053ddd, a two-level table load: the owned target's own word at displacement 0x0, then the word at displacement 0x4 of whatever that named. The slot's type is the persisted record's own void (__thiscall *)(OpaqueBeamTarget *). The concrete implementation behind it is a property of the owned target's type and is not named, because nothing in this body identifies it.

function_extent.body_end_note: the 23 instructions occupy 0x01053db0..0x01053dfb inclusive, which is 0x4c = 76 bytes: the terminator at 0x01053df9 is `RET 0x4` (C2 04 00) and its last byte is 0x01053dfb, so the bridge's body_end 0x01053dfb and body_span_bytes 76 are the byte extent and agree with the listing; the last INSTRUCTION starts at 0x01053df9. The four 0xCC int3 pad bytes begin at 0x01053dfc, outside the 76-byte body, which is why an 80-byte read returns CCCCCCCC after it. Re-read from the bridge at 0x01053dfb: 00 CC CC CC CC.

convention_derivation: receiver placement: PUSH ESI at 0x01053db0 lowers ESP by four, so the operand of `MOV ESI,dword ptr [ESP + 0x8]` at 0x01053db1 is entry-ESP + 0x4. The receiver is the first STACK argument, not ECX.

incoming ECX is dead: nothing reads it before 0x01053db5 overwrites it. A __thiscall receiver would have to be read before it could be dereferenced and this one is never dereferenced. __thiscall is refuted by the listing, and it is the persisted record's own candidate list ('__stdcall', '__thiscall') that the bytes choose between.

cleanup: the terminator is `RET 0x4` = C2 04 00 in the raw bytes, an immediate of four, so the callee pops exactly one 4-byte slot. Under GCC -m32 __attribute__((stdcall)) on a one-pointer prototype emits `ret $4`, verified in the compiled object; __attribute__((thiscall)) would define a hidden second parameter and change the modelled arity.
corroboration: no instruction in the body is a PUSH of an ordinary argument, so the one popped word is the only argument that exists.
observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: ESI (MOV ESI,[ESP + 0x8] at 0x01053db1; every receiver access goes through that alias, and 0x01053ddf reloads ECX from it)
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: The live decompilation is emitted under a literal 'WARNING: Unknown calling convention' banner and the record carries ghidra_calling_convention_signal=no_information with ghidra_parameter_count=3. observed_original_abi.dispatch: abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls=1, call_offsets=[] and vtable_shaped_loads=0; the listing's single indirect transfer is `CALL EDX` at 0x01053ddd, a register transfer, which is why a bracket-only detector reports vtable_shaped_loads=0

mechanics.body_shape: save ESI; take the receiver from the first stack slot; read the receiver's word at displacement 0x124 and, if it is non-null, mark the pointed-to object through an ECX-receiver call; re-read the same word and, if it is still non-null, clear it, load the pointed-to object's own word at displacement 0, load the word at displacement 0x4 of that, and call it with the pointer in ECX; then evaluate the gate on every return, optionally run a two-call relationship path, write the constant byte 0x1 to the result and return popping one word

receiver_displacement.0x124: read at 0x01053db5 and again at 0x01053dc4, written with the immediate 0 at 0x01053dce. This is the only displacement this body's own listing reads or writes on the receiver, and no record names the member it is. The three accesses are three separate instructions at three addresses; the second is a genuine memory read and not a reuse of the register the first loaded.

owned_target_displacements.0x0: read at 0x01053dd8 as a bare [ECX], i.e. the word at offset zero of the object the receiver's 0x124 word points at
owned_target_displacements.0x4: read at 0x01053dda, but from the object 0x01053dd8 named, not from the target. The two loads are of two different objects and the model test proves which by planting a decoy at the target's own 0x4.

mechanics.base_adjustment: none. The body forms no adjusted address: every operand is either a displacement on ESI or a two-level table load, and no LEA or ADD appears.
mechanics.null_behavior: A zero word at the receiver's 0x124 takes JZ 0x01053ddf at 0x01053dbd, so the mark, the clear and the dispatch are all skipped and the slot is left exactly as found. The gate call at 0x01053de1 and everything downstream still run.
mechanics.second_null_behavior: A word that is non-null at 0x01053db5 but null at 0x01053dc4 takes JZ 0x01053ddf at 0x01053dcc, so only the clear and the dispatch are skipped. The listing does not say the mark can null the slot; the second test tolerates it and the model is written so that either behaviour is representable.
gate_evaluation: 0x01053ddf MOV ECX,ESI then 0x01053de1 CALL 0x0104cd50: the gate receiver is the receiver word, reloaded from ESI, not the owned target. Nothing is pushed.
Reached from the entry, from 0x01053dbd and from 0x01053dcc, so it runs on every return.

0x01053de7 TEST AL,AL / 0x01053de9 JZ 0x01053df7: the test is on the gate's result byte, so any non-zero byte takes the branch. The branch is not the returned value; its target is the instruction after the reset.
relationship_path: 0x01053deb CALL 0x00b3d3c0 with no argument and nothing pushed; the listing contains no PUSH at all.
0x01053df0 MOV ECX,EAX then 0x01053df2 CALL 0x00b78860: the accessor's result becomes the next call's ECX receiver unchanged.
Reached only when the gate byte is non-zero. A clear gate touches no global, because the complete 23-instruction listing names no data-segment address.
mechanics.release_ordering: 0x01053dce is a separate instruction at a lower address than the two table loads and the call, and the dispatch's receiver is a register copy taken before the store, so the slot is already zero when the call runs. The model test reads the slot from inside the dispatched call and requires it to be zero there.

branches.condition: the receiver's word at 0x124 is zero
branches.effect: skip the mark, the clear and the dispatch

branches.condition: the receiver's word at 0x124, re-read, is zero
branches.effect: skip the clear and the dispatch only

branches.condition: the gate's result byte is zero

control_flow.note: Both release branches converge on the single unconditional gate evaluation at 0x01053ddf, so the gate and the relationship path run on every return, whether or not a target was owned. All three targets lie inside the body span 0x01053db0..0x01053df9.

virtual_dispatch.form: MOV EAX,[ECX] / MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x4] / CALL EDX, with the owned target in ECX
virtual_dispatch.note: This is the only indirect transfer in the body. Its table is the owned sub-object's own, never the receiver's, so the concrete implementation is a property of the owned target's type and cannot be named from this body. The record's six vtable associations are transitive classifier artefacts and are not used as evidence: dependencies.vtable_reference_count is 0.

return_semantics.kind: one byte written into AL, constant on every reachable path
return_semantics.evidence: 0x01053df7 MOV AL,0x1 is the only instruction in the body that writes the result byte, and it executes on every path: nothing between 0x01053de1 and it branches around it, and 0x01053de9's target IS 0x01053df7.
return_semantics.ownership: The body performs no reference acquisition of its own beyond the dispatch it makes, and no acquisition or release semantics are claimed for the object that dispatch reaches. Whether the 0x124 word is owned, borrowed or a smart handle is not established by any record for this target.
return_semantics.lifetime: not applicable to the returned byte. The receiver's 0x124 word is cleared at 0x01053dce before the dispatch, so the receiver holds no pointer to it while the dispatch runs. Whether anything extends that object's lifetime is outside this body.
return_semantics.declared_type_rationale: std::uint8_t, not bool. The machine fixes a one-byte write of the constant 0x1 and fixes nothing else about the result: the upper three bytes of EAX are whatever the last executed call left there. The persisted abi record's 'return_semantics' prose ('Unconditional success'), ghidra_function's return_type 'bool' and abi_derived.return.type null are three different renderings of the same byte, and two of them are interpretations. This package takes the measurement.

record_contradictions.record_claim: abi_derived.receiver = {bounds_only: true, confidence: UNKNOWN, distinct_offsets: 0, max_offset: null, offsets: [], present: null, reason: 'ecx_reassigned_before_deref', register: null, shape: null, written_through: 0}. record_contradictions.machine_claim: The body accesses the receiver's word at displacement 0x124 three times: MOV ECX,[ESI + 0x124] at 0x01053db5, the same load again at 0x01053dc4, and MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x124],0 at 0x01053dce. Confirmed independently by /disassemble_function and by /read_memory (hex 8b8e24010000 appears twice and c7862401000000000000 once).
record_contradictions.verdict: the record is refuted; the machine governs
record_contradictions.why_the_record_is_wrong: The abstention reason names the symptom and not the cause. ECX is indeed reassigned before it is dereferenced, but ECX was never the receiver: it is dead on entry and is first used as scratch. The deriver's rule keys on ECX, so a body whose receiver arrives on the stack is invisible to it. The record's own observation list also has no memory event for any of the three accesses at all: 0x01053db5 appears only as obs-0005, a REG_WRITE to ECX, with no displacement recorded.
record_contradictions.consequence_for_the_checks: FIELDS/OFFSETS cannot reach a PASS arm for this target. With receiver.register null the grounded arms are unreachable, and the receiver-agnostic absence arm is excluded precisely because the complete, fully-parsed listing does contain memory operands. The honest verdict is WARN for a span that declares its displacements and NOT_AVAILABLE for one that does not; this package declares them, so it gets WARN with a reason that is literally true ('its ABI record names no receiver register to check them against'). This is reported, not worked around.

record_contradictions.record_claim: abi_derived.stack_arguments.slots[0] = {entry_offset: 'entry_ESP+0x4', observed: true, read: false, written: false, size: 4, resolved key 4}.
record_contradictions.machine_claim: That slot is read. 0x01053db1 `MOV ESI,dword ptr [ESP + 0x8]` is the only stack read in the body, and after the PUSH ESI at 0x01053db0 it is exactly entry-ESP + 0x4. The value it yields is the base of all three receiver accesses and the argument of the gate call.
record_contradictions.verdict: the record contradicts itself, and the machine settles it
record_contradictions.why: The same sub-record already contains the observation that refutes it: obs-0003 is {kind: 'STACK_SLOT_READ', base: 'ESP', disp: 8, key: 4, resolved: true, size: 4} at 0x01053db1. Its own resolver computed key 4 -- the correct entry offset -- and the projection above then reports read: false for that key. Both statements cannot be true of the same instruction.
record_contradictions.note: This is why the persisted abi category (hidden_this false, 'the receiver is passed as the first stack argument and the callee pops it') and the derived abi_derived category (receiver undetermined, convention null) disagree: cross_validation.agreement is already false on the record, for this reason.

unresolved_questions: Which member of the receiver is the word at displacement 0x124? The listing proves the displacement, the three accesses and the clear; no record says what the member is called, whether it is owned, borrowed or a smart handle, or what type it really has. The model reads it as a pointer only because 0x01053dd8 dereferences it.

Can the callee at 0x00cb3c70 change the receiver's word at 0x124? The listing re-reads and re-tests the slot three instructions after the call, which tolerates it, and its own body is only `MOV byte ptr [ECX + 0x155],0x1 / RET` so there is no evidence either way. The second test is therefore modelled as a plain re-read guard, and the model test exercises both behaviours.

What is the receiver's total size? The largest displacement this body's own listing touches on the receiver is 0x124, so 0x128 is the smallest extent covering its accesses and nothing more. The prior package asserts 0x178, resting on the +0x174 access that happens inside 0x0104cd50's body; no record for this target gives a size, so none is claimed here.

What is behind the table word at displacement 0x4? The body proves the two-level shape, the displacement and the ECX-receiver shape of the callee. It does not identify the implementation, the owning class or the slot index, and calling it a refcount release would be an inference from the null-then-release idiom rather than an observed decrement.

Which interface does this virtual override, and what are its three .rdata pointer sites? fan_in is 0 and the callers list is empty; the six vtable ids on the record are transitive classifier associations with vtable_reference_count 0. No RTTI and no vtable pass exist for this binary.

Why is a virtual whose receiver is passed on the stack and popped by the callee compiled the way MSVC compiles a member function? A pointer-to-member trampoline taking self explicitly, a __stdcall free function reached through a hand-built table, and a mismatched declaration in the original headers all compile to these bytes, and nothing in this body or in any record for this target distinguishes them. __stdcall is the smallest declaration that reproduces the observed machine, not a claim about how the original was written.

What is the semantic role of the whole sequence? The body releases whatever the receiver's 0x124 word points at when the gate byte is set, and returns a constant. Nothing in any record for this target says what the owned object represents, what the gate bit means, or what the relationship path accomplishes, so none of it is claimed.

conditions: The original process is driven to a state where the receiver's word at displacement 0x124 is non-null, and the entry is reached through one of its .rdata function pointers rather than a direct call, since fan_in is 0.

The pointer at that word is captured, together with the two words the body reads through it (the object's own word at 0x0 and the table word at 0x4), so the two-level shape can be confirmed against a live object rather than a fixture.
A trace records the value at receiver + 0x124 both before and after the call to 0x00cb3c70, which is the only way to settle whether the second test at 0x01053dcc is reachable in practice.

The argument the caller pushes and the stack delta across the call are captured, which is the only way to confirm the one-word callee-popped surface against a real caller rather than against the bytes alone.
The byte left in AL at 0x01053df9 is compared against the reconstructed signature.

validation.compile_result: clean, zero warnings under -Wall -Wextra -Werror. The header additionally compiles clean standalone, and both translation units also pass clang++ -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -fsyntax-only.
validation.abi_fidelity_result: the compiled entry's terminator is `c2 04 00  ret $0x4`, byte-identical in form to the machine's C2 04 00 at 0x01053df9. The register and stack schedule of the body is GCC's, not a hand-written replica, so no claim of instruction-for-instruction codegen identity is made; what is claimed is the argument surface, the callee-side cleanup, the transfer set and the branch structure.
validation.mutation_result: 9 mutants, 9 caught, 0 survived. Each mutant is an independent single-instruction-level break of the reconstruction, and each was killed by a named assertion in the model test rather than by a crash or a compile error: dropping the second load of the 0x124 word; moving the 0x124 clear to after the indirect call; returning the gate byte instead of the constant; inverting the 0x01053de9 branch; applying the 0x4 displacement to the target instead of the table (and reading the table's 0x0 instead of its 0x4); declaring cdecl in both the header and the definition so the callee stops popping; handing the dispatch the receiver instead of the owned target; reading the owned word at 0x120 instead of 0x124; and gating on the owned target instead of the receiver. The baseline is re-checked first in every run and must be clean for any of the results above to mean anything.

expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS, and this is a real adjudication rather than a fallback. The xref export and the complete 23-instruction listing independently name the same four direct targets, and the source span names exactly those four. The span binds because the entry symbol carries both the VA token and the record name's last component.
expected_reasons.GLOBALS: PASS on an evidenced absence: the complete listing names no data-segment address and the span names none. The body reaches the relationship state only through the accessor at 0x01053deb, so the accessor callee's own global is not this body's global.
expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: PASS, and it is doing real work. The span states three hexadecimal literals (0x124, 0x4, 0x1) and every one of them appears in the fully-parsed 23-instruction listing, so the two receiver displacements and the result byte are each corroborated against the machine. This is why the displacements are written literally inside the span rather than hidden behind named constants: a span stating no literal takes the trivially-passing arm of this check and is checked for nothing.
expected_reasons.CONTROL FLOW: PASS. All three conditional branch targets lie inside the body span 0x01053db0..0x01053df9, so the branch graph is closed inside it. The branch keyword count is reported in the detail and is explicitly not part of the verdict.
expected_reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: PASS, and here the source side is adjudicated too, not merely tolerated. The machine parse consumed 23 of 23 instructions with 0 unparsed, the dispatch record independently counts 1 indirect transfer, the single site is a two-level table load, and the displacement the span declares for its slot (0x4) is among the machine slot displacements. The record's six vtable associations are not used and prove nothing.
expected_reasons.ABI: WARN, and it is not fixable from this package. The check reports the DERIVED record's own confidence, which is UNKNOWN because the deriver abstained (see C-DERIVER-READS-NO-OWNED-WORD). The source declares __stdcall and the bytes support it, but the check asks whether the machine-derived oracle is proven, and it is not. No source edit can move it.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: WARN, and it is a verdict about the evidence, not about this reconstruction. The span declares two displacements (0x124 and 0x4) that the complete listing does show, but the machine-derived receiver record names no receiver register, so there is no machine bound to check them against and no arm can pass. Two honest consequences are recorded rather than smoothed over: first, the machine demonstrably performs the field access that the record denies, so the residual WARN understates what is known; second, this package's choice to declare its displacements is what turns NOT_AVAILABLE into WARN, and NOT_AVAILABLE is disqualifying for the aggregate while WARN is not. Declaring them is the more informative choice, not the more flattering one.
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: WARN, and it is structurally forced. The persisted abi record carries a return_semantics prose string, which the check compares by string equality against the span's declared return type; no C++ type can equal that sentence, so any reconstruction of this target lands here. Declaring bool instead of std::uint8_t would not change the verdict, and uint8_t is the more defensible of the two because the byte and its constant value are measured while 'true' is an interpretation.
